claim: John Sulston and colleagues elucidated the 1340 cells generated throughout the embryogenesis of the nematode C. elegans, leading to a hatched worm with 558 cells, each with a described name, lineage, and fate.
source: John Sulston and colleagues elucidated the 1340 cells generated throughout the embryogenesis of the nematode C. elegans, leading to a hatched worm with 558 cells, each with a described name, lineage, and fate (Sulston et al., 1983).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Sulston et al., 1983, which is a reference to published work.

claim: The C. elegans cell lineage is delineated into a germ-line lineage (P) and five 'founder' somatic cell lineages (AB, MS, E, C, and D) that each have characteristic cell cycle timings.
source: The cell lineage is delineated into a germ-line lineage – P – and five 'founder' somatic cell lineages – AB, MS, E, C, and D – that each have characteristic cell cycle timings (Deppe et al., 1978) and cell fates (Figure 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Deppe et al., 1978, and reference to Figure 1a.

claim: All founder cell lineages are present by the 28-cell stage, when gastrulation initiates.
source: All founder cell lineages are present by the 28-cell stage, when gastrulation initiates, and by the 102-cell stage the progeny of most of the cells have a single fate.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about C. elegans development.

claim: By the 102-cell stage the progeny of most of the cells have a single fate.
source: All founder cell lineages are present by the 28-cell stage, when gastrulation initiates, and by the 102-cell stage the progeny of most of the cells have a single fate.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about C. elegans development.

claim: There are 934 annotated transcription factors in C. elegans.
source: Overall, there are 934 annotated TFs in C. elegans, with 40% having experimentally studied DNA-binding specificities (Narasimhan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Narasimhan et al., 2015.

claim: 40% of C. elegans transcription factors have experimentally studied DNA-binding specificities.
source: Overall, there are 934 annotated TFs in C. elegans, with 40% having experimentally studied DNA-binding specificities (Narasimhan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Narasimhan et al., 2015.

claim: The study analyzed 840 cells from 38 embryos up to the 102-cell stage.
source: Overall, we studied 840 cells from 38 embryos up to the 102-cell stage, collecting all or most cells of each embryo (Figure 1b and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental data collected in the study.

claim: Embryo-to-embryo variation could be efficiently normalized by standardizing each gene's expression across all cells collected from the same embryo.
source: Analyzing the transcriptomes, we found that embryo-to-embryo variation could be efficiently normalized by standardizing each gene's expression across all cells collected from the same embryo (see Methods), and this is another benefit of the manual collection approach.
evidence: This claim is based on the analysis performed in the study.

claim: Cells from early stages occupy the center of the dimensional reduction map while cells from later stages occupy the periphery.
source: A dimensional reduction map of the examined cells (Figure 1b) reveals the unfolding of development with cells from the early stages occupying the center while cells from later stages occupy the periphery.
evidence: This claim is supported by the dimensional reduction analysis shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Cells followed developmental trajectories according to their founder cell origin.
source: We found that cells followed developmental trajectories according to their founder cell origin, each identified by the expression of genes known to be expressed in a lineage-specific manner: ceh-51 (MS), elt-7 (E), pal-1 (C,D and P), pes-1 (D), and nos-2 (P) (Figure 1c; Broitman-Maduro et al., 2009; Hunter and Kenyon, 1996; Lee et al., 2017; Maduro and Rothman, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1c and citations to previous work.

claim: ceh-51 is expressed in a lineage-specific manner in the MS lineage.
source: We found that cells followed developmental trajectories according to their founder cell origin, each identified by the expression of genes known to be expressed in a lineage-specific manner: ceh-51 (MS), elt-7 (E), pal-1 (C,D and P), pes-1 (D), and nos-2 (P) (Figure 1c; Broitman-Maduro et al., 2009; Hunter and Kenyon, 1996; Lee et al., 2017; Maduro and Rothman, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work and data in Figure 1c.

claim: elt-7 is expressed in a lineage-specific manner in the E lineage.
source: We found that cells followed developmental trajectories according to their founder cell origin, each identified by the expression of genes known to be expressed in a lineage-specific manner: ceh-51 (MS), elt-7 (E), pal-1 (C,D and P), pes-1 (D), and nos-2 (P) (Figure 1c; Broitman-Maduro et al., 2009; Hunter and Kenyon, 1996; Lee et al., 2017; Maduro and Rothman, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work and data in Figure 1c.

claim: pal-1 is expressed in a lineage-specific manner in the C, D, and P lineages.
source: We found that cells followed developmental trajectories according to their founder cell origin, each identified by the expression of genes known to be expressed in a lineage-specific manner: ceh-51 (MS), elt-7 (E), pal-1 (C,D and P), pes-1 (D), and nos-2 (P) (Figure 1c; Broitman-Maduro et al., 2009; Hunter and Kenyon, 1996; Lee et al., 2017; Maduro and Rothman, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work and data in Figure 1c.

claim: pes-1 is expressed in a lineage-specific manner in the D lineage.
source: We found that cells followed developmental trajectories according to their founder cell origin, each identified by the expression of genes known to be expressed in a lineage-specific manner: ceh-51 (MS), elt-7 (E), pal-1 (C,D and P), pes-1 (D), and nos-2 (P) (Figure 1c; Broitman-Maduro et al., 2009; Hunter and Kenyon, 1996; Lee et al., 2017; Maduro and Rothman, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work and data in Figure 1c.

claim: nos-2 is expressed in a lineage-specific manner in the P lineage.
source: We found that cells followed developmental trajectories according to their founder cell origin, each identified by the expression of genes known to be expressed in a lineage-specific manner: ceh-51 (MS), elt-7 (E), pal-1 (C,D and P), pes-1 (D), and nos-2 (P) (Figure 1c; Broitman-Maduro et al., 2009; Hunter and Kenyon, 1996; Lee et al., 2017; Maduro and Rothman, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work and data in Figure 1c.

claim: The founder cell lineage trajectories are oriented according to cell fates, with similar cell fates converging between lineages.
source: As also observed by other studies (Packer et al., 2019), the founder cell lineage trajectories are oriented according to cell fates, with similar cell fates converging between lineages (Figure 1b and d): the cells of the ecto-mesoderm producing C lineage formed a bi-lobed cloud with the muscle part adjacent to that of the MS and D lineages.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 1b and d, and a citation to Packer et al., 2019.

claim: The cells of the ecto-mesoderm producing C lineage formed a bi-lobed cloud with the muscle part adjacent to that of the MS and D lineages.
source: As also observed by other studies (Packer et al., 2019), the founder cell lineage trajectories are oriented according to cell fates, with similar cell fates converging between lineages (Figure 1b and d): the cells of the ecto-mesoderm producing C lineage formed a bi-lobed cloud with the muscle part adjacent to that of the MS and D lineages.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 1b and d.

claim: MS cells that will form the pharynx orient toward the pharynx producing portion of the AB lineage.
source: Similarly, MS cells that will form the pharynx orient toward the pharynx producing portion of the AB lineage.
evidence: This claim is supported by data analysis in the study.

claim: The study organized embryos into eight developmental stages: 1-, 2-, 4-, 8-, 15-, 28-, 51-, and 102-cell stages.
source: In order to infer the precise identity of each cell, we first organized the embryos into eight developmental stages: the 1-, 2-, 4-, 8-, 15-, 28-, 51-, and 102-cell stages (Figure 1a).
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: The identified clusters contain cells from each of the individual embryos, confirming that embryo to embryo gene expression variation is minimal relative to the coherence of the cell states within an embryo.
source: The identified clusters contain cells from each of the individual embryos, thus confirming our underlying assumption that embryo to embryo gene expression variation is minimal relative to the coherence of the cell states within an embryo.
evidence: This claim is based on the clustering analysis performed in the study.

claim: F19F10.1 is a previously uncharacterized ets-factor that is expressed in the posterior daughter cell through 2-cell cycle divisions.
source: Studying F19F10.1 by single-molecule fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH), we found that this previously uncharacterized ets-factor is expressed in the posterior daughter cell through 2-cell cycle divisions (Figure 2c).
evidence: This claim is supported by FISH data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: 5433 genes were identified as being differentially expressed within a stage, collectively across all of the stages.
source: We identified 5433 genes as being differentially expressed within a stage, collectively across all of the stages (see Methods).
evidence: This claim describes the results of differential expression analysis.

claim: 395 transcription factors are differentially expressed during the period of cell specification studied.
source: Of these, 395 are TFs during this period of cell specification (Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This claim is based on the analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: The study describes 119 cell identities with distinct transcriptome profiles.
source: Altogether we describe 119-cell identities with distinct transcriptome profiles, which by stage, are as follows: 1 (1-cell), 2 (2-cell), 4 (4-cell), 6 (8-cell), 11 (15-cell), 20 (28-cell), 38 (51-cell), and 37 (102-cell), with 64 of these representing equivalence groups of at least two cell states (Figure 2d, Supplementary file 5, and Figure 2—figure supplement 8).
evidence: This claim summarizes the cell identity analysis performed in the study.

claim: 64 of the 119 cell identities represent equivalence groups of at least two cell states.
source: Altogether we describe 119-cell identities with distinct transcriptome profiles, which by stage, are as follows: 1 (1-cell), 2 (2-cell), 4 (4-cell), 6 (8-cell), 11 (15-cell), 20 (28-cell), 38 (51-cell), and 37 (102-cell), with 64 of these representing equivalence groups of at least two cell states (Figure 2d, Supplementary file 5, and Figure 2—figure supplement 8).
evidence: This claim is based on the cell identity analysis.

claim: Each cell state has an average of seven replicate cells.
source: For each cell state that we assigned, we have an average of seven replicate cells (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This claim describes the sampling depth of the study.

claim: The delay between GFP expression and mRNA detection is expected as previously described.
source: The delay between the GFP expression and the mRNA detected here is expected as previously described (Murray et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Murray et al., 2012.

claim: The ABplppp cell differentially expresses 14 transcription factors, including seven homeobox domain TFs.
source: As an example, the 'ABplppp' cell differentially expresses 14 TFs according to our analysis, including seven homeobox domain (HD) TFs, though overall HDs only account for 11% of the TFs (Figure 3a).
evidence: This claim is based on the analysis shown in Figure 3a.

claim: Homeobox domain TFs account for 11% of all transcription factors.
source: As an example, the 'ABplppp' cell differentially expresses 14 TFs according to our analysis, including seven homeobox domain (HD) TFs, though overall HDs only account for 11% of the TFs (Figure 3a).
evidence: This claim is based on the analysis of TF families.

claim: The enrichment of seven homeobox domain TFs in the ABplppp cell has a significance of p=0.00015.
source: We used the hypergeometric distribution to compute a significance of p=0.00015 for this overlap, given the overall number of TFs and the number of HD and 'ABplppp' TFs.
evidence: This claim is based on statistical analysis using the hypergeometric distribution.

claim: Only two of the 69 TFs expressed by the Eala cell are homeobox domain TFs, representing a significant depletion (p=0.01).
source: Conversely, only two of the 69 TFs expressed by the Eala cell are HDs, a significant depletion (p=0.01, hypergeometric distribution).
evidence: This claim is based on statistical analysis using the hypergeometric distribution.

claim: Homeobox domain TFs are enriched in the 51-cell stage, particularly in the ABp lineage.
source: Figure 3b shows the overall pattern of enrichments and depletions of HDs across all of the examined cells, indicating enrichment of HDs in the 51-cell stage, in particular in the ABp lineage, and depletion in the E lineage.
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 3b.

claim: Homeobox domain TFs are depleted in the E lineage.
source: Figure 3b shows the overall pattern of enrichments and depletions of HDs across all of the examined cells, indicating enrichment of HDs in the 51-cell stage, in particular in the ABp lineage, and depletion in the E lineage.
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 3b.

claim: GATA type zinc factors are enriched in the E lineage and some AB cells.
source: For the GATA type zinc factors we found enrichment in the E lineage, as well as some of the AB cells (Figure 3c).
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 3c.

claim: TF families showed significant enrichments across lineages and developmental stages.
source: Examining the pattern of such biases, we found that TF families showed significant enrichments across lineages and developmental stages (Figure 3d–e).
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 3d-e.

claim: Four TF gene families are enriched in the AB lineage: the T-box domain, the helix-loop-helix DNA-binding domain, the homeodomain, and the high mobility group box domain.
source: Four TF gene families are enriched in the AB lineage: the T-box domain, the helix-loop-helix (HLH) DNA-binding domain, the HD domain, and the high mobility group (HMG) box domain (Figure 3d).
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 3d.

claim: In the 28-cell stage, each of the 16 AB cells contains expression of at least one homeodomain gene, with 8 distinct cell state patterns.
source: Studying this in more detail, we observed that in the 28-cell stage, each of the 16 AB cells contains expression of at least one homeodomain gene, with 8 distinct cell state patterns (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 4a.

claim: ceh-43 is expressed in nine of the sixteen AB cells at the 28-cell stage in a complex pattern.
source: For example, ceh-43 is expressed in nine of the sixteen AB cells at the 28-cell stage in a complex pattern (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Continuous symmetry breaking does not appear to be a mechanism by which differential expression is generally established.
source: Thus, continuous symmetry breaking (Zacharias and Murray, 2016) does not appear to be a mechanism by which differential expression is generally established.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observed expression patterns and includes a citation to Zacharias and Murray, 2016.

claim: The homeodomain genes expressed in each lineage revealed dorsal-ventral stripes along the anterior-posterior axis at the 28-cell stage.
source: Studying the 28-cell stage, we found that the homeodomain genes expressed in each lineage revealed dorsal-ventral stripes along the anterior-posterior axis (Figure 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by the spatial analysis shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The ceh-43-expressing cells, deriving from distinct AB sub-lineages, are physically proximate.
source: For example, the ceh-43-expressing cells, deriving from distinct AB sub-lineages, are physically proximate.
evidence: This claim is based on the spatial mapping analysis.

claim: At the 51-cell stage, 4 new homeodomain genes are expressed in the AB lineage.
source: At the 51-cell stage, 4 new homeodomain genes are expressed in the AB lineage, and again position along the anterior-posterior axis correlates with gene expression.
evidence: This claim is based on the analysis of gene expression at the 51-cell stage.

claim: Position along the anterior-posterior axis correlates with gene expression at the 51-cell stage.
source: At the 51-cell stage, 4 new homeodomain genes are expressed in the AB lineage, and again position along the anterior-posterior axis correlates with gene expression.
evidence: This claim is based on the spatial analysis of gene expression.

claim: At the 102-cell stage, expression becomes more complicated as the AB lineage forms an external shell around the gastrulating non-AB cells.
source: In the 102-cell stage, expression becomes more complicated as the AB lineage forms an external shell around the gastrulating non-AB cells.
evidence: This claim is based on the analysis of the 102-cell stage.

claim: For the MS lineage, ceh-32 and ceh-51 are in the anterior and posterior, respectively.
source: For the MS lineage, ceh-32 and ceh-51 are in the anterior and posterior, respectively, while for the C lineage vab-7 (even-skipped) and hmbx-1 are in the anterior and posterior, respectively.
evidence: This claim is based on the spatial analysis of gene expression in the MS lineage.

claim: For the C lineage, vab-7 (even-skipped) and hmbx-1 are in the anterior and posterior, respectively.
source: For the MS lineage, ceh-32 and ceh-51 are in the anterior and posterior, respectively, while for the C lineage vab-7 (even-skipped) and hmbx-1 are in the anterior and posterior, respectively.
evidence: This claim is based on the spatial analysis of gene expression in the C lineage.

claim: Distinct regionalization codes occur across the embryonic sub-lineages.
source: We thus provide evidence that distinct regionalization codes occur across the embryonic sub-lineages.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion based on the spatial analysis of gene expression patterns.

claim: C. elegans genes nos-1,2 (nanos) and puf genes (pumilio) are restricted to the primary germ cell lineage.
source: We found that the C. elegans genes such as nos-1,2 (nanos) and puf genes (pumilio) which are maternal genes in both systems are restricted to the primary germ cell lineage in C. elegans (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: Gap and pair-rule genes, such as pal-1 (caudal) and cwn-1 (wg), show C lineage and sub-lineage restriction, respectively.
source: Moreover, gap and pair-rule genes, such as pal-1 (caudal) and cwn-1 (wg), show C lineage and sub-lineage restriction, respectively (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: While Drosophila patterning follows in a lineage-independent manner, in C. elegans, lineage dependency is coincident with specific expression of patterning genes across the founder cell lineages.
source: Thus, it is evident that while Drosophila patterning follows in a lineage-independent manner, in C. elegans, lineage dependency is coincident with specific expression of patterning genes across the founder cell lineages.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion based on the comparison of patterning mechanisms between Drosophila and C. elegans.

claim: Three of the homeodomain genes whose expression was described (ceh-13, php-3, and nob-1) are members of the HOX sub-family.
source: Three of the homeodomain genes whose expression we have described – ceh-13, php-3, and nob-1 (Figure 4) – are members of the HOX sub-family, known to provide regionalization during embryogenesis in bilaterians (Carroll et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 4 and a citation to Carroll et al., 2004.

claim: HOX genes are known to provide regionalization during embryogenesis in bilaterians.
source: Three of the homeodomain genes whose expression we have described – ceh-13, php-3, and nob-1 (Figure 4) – are members of the HOX sub-family, known to provide regionalization during embryogenesis in bilaterians (Carroll et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Carroll et al., 2004.

claim: Expression of HOX genes transcends the founder lineages and patterns the posterior region in multiple lineages.
source: Indeed, we observed that expression of these HOX genes transcends the founder lineages and patterns the posterior region in multiple lineages (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 4.

claim: 51 other homeodomain genes likely pattern the lineages and set up locations in the embryo.
source: However, we find 51 other homeodomain genes that likely pattern the lineages and set up locations in the embryo.
evidence: This claim is based on the analysis of homeodomain gene expression and involves speculation about their function.

claim: C. elegans has 97 homeodomain genes.
source: This is a large genetic repertoire relative to Drosophila (97 genes in C. elegans, relative to 104 in Drosophila) despite the higher complexity of the latter in terms of cell types and total number of cells.
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge of the genomic repertoire of C. elegans.

claim: Drosophila has 104 homeodomain genes.
source: This is a large genetic repertoire relative to Drosophila (97 genes in C. elegans, relative to 104 in Drosophila) despite the higher complexity of the latter in terms of cell types and total number of cells.
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge of the genomic repertoire of Drosophila.

claim: In species where regionalization is under lineage control, as opposed to morphogen gradients, there is apparently a greater necessity for distinct positional systems across distinct sub-lineages.
source: Thus, in species where regionalization is under lineage control, as opposed to morphogen gradients, there is apparently a greater necessity for distinct positional systems across distinct sub-lineages – here the founder cell lineages.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the comparison of C. elegans and Drosophila.

claim: Lineage-specific gene expression stripes suggest that developmental patterning mechanisms may not be restricted to segmented organisms but is rather a universal feature of animal embryogenesis.
source: We find lineage-specific gene expression stripes (Figure 4), suggesting that such a developmental patterning mechanism may not be restricted to segmented organisms but is rather a universal feature of animal embryogenesis.
evidence: This claim is a speculation based on the observed gene expression patterns.

claim: The centrality of homeodomain genes to the patterning system highlights the adaptability of this TF family to both lineage-dependent and position-dependent functions.
source: The centrality of homeodomain genes to this system highlights the adaptability of this TF family to both lineage-dependent and position-dependent functions.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observed role of homeodomain genes.

claim: The C. elegans embryo is patterned by a juxtaposition of distinct lineage-specific gene regulatory programs each with a unique encoding of cell location and fate.
source: These results suggest that the C. elegans embryo is patterned by a juxtaposition of distinct lineage-specific gene regulatory programs each with a unique encoding of cell location and fate.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: The use of homologous gene regulatory patterning codes suggests a deep homology of cell fate specification programs across diverse modes of development.
source: This use of homologous gene regulatory patterning codes suggests a deep homology of cell fate specification programs across diverse modes of development.
evidence: This claim is a speculation about evolutionary conservation based on the findings.

claim: Developmental toolkit genes constitute the genomic repertoire that underlies the pathways patterning the organism.
source: Developmental toolkit genes constitute the genomic repertoire that underlies the pathways patterning the organism (Carroll, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Carroll, 2008.

claim: Developmental toolkit genes are generally involved in signaling transduction modules and transcription factors.
source: These genes are generally involved in signaling transduction modules and transcription factors (TFs) (Degnan et al., 2009; Gerhart, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Degnan et al., 2009 and Gerhart, 1999.

claim: The C. elegans endoderm is specified by a cascade of TFs operating sequentially.
source: For example, the Caenorhabditis elegans endoderm is specified by a cascade of TFs operating sequentially (Maduro and Rothman, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Maduro and Rothman, 2002.

claim: Segmentation in the Drosophila embryo is established by morphogens within a syncytium, and the subsequent action of the gap, pair-rule, and segment polarity genes.
source: In Drosophila, classic work has shown that segmentation in the embryo is established by morphogens within a syncytium, and the subsequent action of the gap, pair-rule, and segment polarity genes.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about Drosophila development.

claim: The classic Drosophila segmentation model does not translate directly to species that lack a syncytium, such as C. elegans, where cell fate is specified by cell-autonomous cell lineage programs and their inter-signaling.
source: This classic model however does not translate directly to species that lack a syncytium – such as Caenorhabditis elegans – where cell fate is specified by cell-autonomous cell lineage programs and their inter-signaling.
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge about differences in developmental mechanisms.

claim: Previous single-cell RNA-Seq studies in C. elegans have analyzed cells from a mixed suspension of cells from many embryos to study late differentiation stages.
source: Previous single-cell RNA-Seq studies in C. elegans have analyzed cells from a mixed suspension of cells from many embryos to study late differentiation stages, or individual early stage embryos to study early gene expression in the embryo.
evidence: This claim describes previous research approaches.

claim: Previous single-cell RNA-Seq studies in C. elegans have analyzed individual early stage embryos to study early gene expression in the embryo.
source: Previous single-cell RNA-Seq studies in C. elegans have analyzed cells from a mixed suspension of cells from many embryos to study late differentiation stages, or individual early stage embryos to study early gene expression in the embryo.
evidence: This claim describes previous research approaches.

claim: The study determined the transcriptomes of the 1- to 102-cell stage to identify 119 embryonic cell states during cell fate specification, including 'equivalence-group' cell identities.
source: To study the intermediate stages of early and late gastrulation (28- to 102-cells stages) missed by these approaches, here we determine the transcriptomes of the 1- to 102-cell stage to identify 119 embryonic cell states during cell fate specification, including 'equivalence-group' cell identities.
evidence: This claim summarizes the main findings of the study.

claim: Gene expression programs are modular according to the sub-cell lineages, each establishing a set of stripes by combinations of transcription factor gene expression across the anterior-posterior axis.
source: We find that gene expression programs are modular according to the sub-cell lineages, each establishing a set of stripes by combinations of transcription factor gene expression across the anterior-posterior axis.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion based on the analysis of gene expression patterns.

claim: Expression of the homeodomain genes establishes a comprehensive lineage-specific positioning system throughout the embryo beginning at the 28-cell stage.
source: In particular, expression of the homeodomain genes establishes a comprehensive lineage-specific positioning system throughout the embryo beginning at the 28-cell stage.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion based on the analysis of homeodomain gene expression.

claim: Genes that segment the entire embryo in Drosophila have orthologs in C. elegans that exhibit sub-lineage-specific expression.
source: Moreover, we find that genes that segment the entire embryo in Drosophila have orthologs in C. elegans that exhibit sub-lineage-specific expression.
evidence: This claim is based on the comparative analysis of gene expression between Drosophila and C. elegans.

claim: Individual embryos were manually dissociated by gentle pipetting through progressively smaller glass-bore pipettes in calcium/magnesium-free EGM.
source: Individual embryos were manually dissociated by gentle pipetting through progressively smaller glass-bore pipettes in calcium/magnesium-free EGM.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental method used.

claim: Cell collection was limited to a 30 min window from the beginning of the dissociation process.
source: Cell collection was limited to a 30 min window from the beginning of the dissociation process.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental protocol.

claim: Individual embryo, multiplexed single-cell RNA-Seq libraries were produced following the CEL-Seq2 protocol.
source: Individual embryo, multiplexed single-cell RNA-Seq libraries were produced following the CEL-Seq2 protocol (Hashimshony et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental method and is supported by a citation to Hashimshony et al., 2016.

claim: RNA molecules were tagged with unique molecular identifiers (UMIs).
source: Briefly, individually harvested cells were barcoded with a reverse transcription reaction, and RNA molecules were tagged with unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) (Kivioja et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental method and is supported by a citation to Kivioja et al., 2011.

claim: Only cells with more than 10,000 mapped reads were included in the analysis.
source: Gene expression values were calculated as UMI-corrected reads normalized to the number of transcripts per 50,000; only cells with more than 10,000 mapped reads were included in the analysis.
evidence: This claim describes the data filtering criteria.

claim: Gene expression was standardized among the cells of an individual embryo such that the mean expression for each gene across the cells of the embryo is 0 and the standard deviation is 1.
source: In order to compare gene expression patterns between embryos, gene expression was first standardized among the cells of an individual embryo (such that the mean expression for each gene across the cells of the embryo is 0 and the standard deviation is 1), and these standardized expression profiles were used for comparisons between embryos.
evidence: This claim describes the data normalization method.

claim: t-SNE was performed on the full dataset using the top 1000 most variable genes according to the Fano factor, with 20 initial dimensions and perplexity set at 50.
source: t-Distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (tSNE) (van der Maaten and Hinton, 2008) was performed on full dataset using the top 1000 most variable genes (according to the Fano factor), with 20 initial dimensions and perplexity set at 50.
evidence: This claim describes the computational method used and includes a citation to van der Maaten and Hinton, 2008.

claim: The complete dataset has been deposited to the NCBI GEO database GSE83523.
source: The complete dataset has been deposited to the NCBI GEO database GSE83523.
evidence: This claim describes data availability.
